idiom_name: generic container View with a @ViewBuilder content closure taking the state
implementation_notes: SwiftUI makes the render function a closure parameter annotated with the result builder: ViewBuilder is documented as 'a custom parameter attribute that constructs views from closures', so a container view declares content: (State) -> Content (or @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content) and invokes it with its own state, while the call site's closure is ordinary SwiftUI view code. The classic component structure is replaced by this generic container plus a closure; keep it when the container owns state or layout, and prefer a plain view plus @State/Bindable when the child markup is fixed. In UIKit the same inversion arrives as closure registrations: UICollectionView.CellRegistration takes a handler that configures each cell for its item, and the diffable data source's cell provider calls it.
pitfalls: The closure is recreated on every re-render of the caller; for expensive subtrees pass Equatable data or wrap the content so SwiftUI can skip recomputation.
Capturing self or state in an escaping closure captures stale values or creates retain cycles; the content closure owns what it captures.
Result-builder closures accept only the statements the builder supports; an unsupported construct fails with an opaque compiler error rather than a clear diagnostic.

variants.name: UIKit cell registration and diffable data source cell provider
variants.idiom_name: UICollectionView.CellRegistration<Cell, Item> handler invoked per item
variants.implementation_notes: UIKit's documented mechanism is a registration object holding a handler closure: CellRegistration is generic over the cell and the item type and its handler receives (cell, indexPath, item) to specify how to configure the content and appearance of that type of cell; the collection view's diffable data source cell provider returns the dequeued, configured cell. The caller therefore supplies the rendering function for every item while the collection view owns recycling and layout - the render prop with cell reuse. Choose it for list and collection screens on UIKit; prefer the SwiftUI closure container for view trees that are not item-shaped.
pitfalls: The docs warn against creating the cell registration inside the cell provider closure: doing so defeats cell reuse and raises an exception on iOS 15 and later.
The handler configures recycled cells, so it must set every relevant property and reset transient state; stale configuration in a reused cell is the classic bug.
The registration's generic parameters must match the data source's item type exactly, or dequeueConfiguredReusableCell cannot find it at runtime.
